title: SLO collaboration: mini-program canvas and pilot checklist
content:
Purpose:
A compact, low-friction program to get 3 product teams through a crawl-walk-run SLO adoption loop in 6 weeks. Not a full orgwide rollout — instead: repeatable mini-pilots that produce observable outcomes, handoffs, and artifacts teams can copy.

Goals (what success looks like for a mini-pilot):
- Each team has 1 service with an agreed SLO (latency or availability) + measured baseline.
- One automated alert or regression check wired into the Console for that SLO.
- Run a canary/traffic experiment asserting the SLO on a small % traffic and capture metrics + incident simulation notes.
- Deliver a 1-page handoff pack (SLO def, owner, runbook link, key dashboards, next steps).

Scope decisions (keep narrow):
- Focus on serving endpoints used by customer-facing flows (generation, embeddings, rerank routes).
- Avoid model-level config changes in the first pilot (no quantization rollouts).
- Use existing telemetry (proxy metrics, request latency histograms, error counters) + one lightweight synthetic check per endpoint.

High-level timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0: intake + quick baseline (1 day intake per team, 2 days baseline run).
- Week 1: SLO definition workshop (half day), agree objectives and SLO owners.
- Week 2: Dashboard + alert config (pairing SRE + product).
- Week 3: Canary cutover + smoke verification.
- Week 4: Incident tabletop + regression check.
- Week 5: Handoff pack + retro + next-phase plan.

Role matrix (minimal):
- SRE lead: runbook template, alert tuning, canary config (Daniel Kim).
- Product owner: define user-impacting thresholds, acceptance criteria (Priya Shah).
- Eng rotation: implement metric tagging + dashboard (team-assigned eng).
- Observability engineer: tracing hooks, sampling guidance (Omar Mendes).
- Program coordinator: schedule, artifact collection, retro facilitation (Ava Martinez).

Pilot recipe (repeatable checklist):
1) Intake form (quick): service name, critical routes, expected p50/p95, recent deploy cadence, owner contact.
2) Baseline run: 72h of traffic, capture latency histogram, error rate, token-level cost impact note.
3) Define SLO: objective (SLO target), SLI (exact metric + window), SLO period, error budget policy. Keep one SLO per service initially.
4) Dashboard: artifact with p50/p95, success-rate over window, error-budget burn chart. Add runbook link.
5) Alerting: primary alert at early burn (e.g., 10% burn in 24h) + mitigation playbook stub.
6) Canary: route 2–5% traffic for 24–48h, collect slice metrics, check rollback criteria.
7) Tabletop: simulate a 30% p95 regression, run through comms + escalation.
8) Handoff pack: single page plus links; include lessons, outstanding risks, proposed SLA if requested.

Tactical notes + shortcuts (to reduce friction):
- Use shared dashboard template in Console (copy+edit).
- For SLI, prefer success-rate or 95th latency depending on product impact. Document the tradeoffs in 2 bullets.
- If telemetry gaps exist, use a short-term synthetic probe (edge-level) instead of instrumenting a deep tracing change.
- Reuse existing incident severity ladder and paging rules; don’t invent new incident levels for pilots.

Runbook handoff skeleton (what must be present):
- SLO definition (metric, target, window)
- Who to page (role, not person)
- Quick mitigation steps (3 bullets)
- Known risky changes that can affect the SLO (deploy patterns, cache flushes, regen jobs)
- Links: dashboard, alert config, recent canary run logs

Communication plan (internal & customer-facing):
- Internal: weekly 30-minute sync during pilot window + demo at week 5 retro. Keep updates in #reliability-pilots slack thread (use summary template).
- Customers: only notify customers if SLO demo impacts >5% of traffic and we activate a mitigation; otherwise keep posture internal.

Artifacts to capture and share:
- Baseline CSV (p50/p95/time) + screenshot of dashboard.
- Canary run log (start/end, % traffic, results).
- Tabletop notes and action items.
- Handoff pack (single page).

Metrics & measurement (simple):
- Primary: SLI measured as "successful requests / total requests" or p95 latency <= threshold.
- Secondary: alert burn rate, mean time to detect (MTTD) in pilot, mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for simulated incident.

Risks & mitigations (quick list):
- Risk: teams over-define SLOs (too strict). Mitigation: default safe SLO templates and coach to pick one signal only.
- Risk: noisy alerts. Mitigation: pair on tuning and set a burn-based alert.
- Risk: telemetry gaps. Mitigation: synthetic probes + backlog ticket to instrument properly.

Sustainability & next steps after pilot:
- If pilot meets goal: convert artifacts into a reusable template in Confluence and promote 3 more teams for Q1 run.
- If pilot fails (major blockers): capture blockers, triage to infra or product depending on root cause, re-run a corrected mini-pilot in 8 weeks.

Notes to self / TODOs (actionable, small):
- [ ] Build dashboard template in Console (Omar) — due 2026-01-22.
- [ ] Draft intake form + Slack workflow (Lina) — due 2026-01-20.
- [ ] Schedule 3 half-day workshops (Ava) — send invites.
- [ ] Create Confluence page stub: /Reliability/Mini-Pilot-Canvas (Ava).

Open questions (triage in Week 0):
- Do we allow teams to pick availability vs latency as SLO type? (recommended: yes, but default latency for user-facing gen routes)
- Can Dedicated customers be included in pilot traffic slices? (legal/data isolation concerns)
- Do we need a separate cost-SLO? (monitoring note: token cost spikes can be correlated but keep separate initially)

Quick wins to reduce friction:
- Pre-built alert rule library with 3 templates (latency p95, success-rate, error-rate burn).
- Standard naming convention for SLO dashboards so program finder can auto-collect.

Record of decisions so far:
- Minimal scope per pilot = 1 SLO, 1 dashboard, 1 runbook, 1 tabletop.
- Canary strategy default = 3% traffic for 48h unless product owner requests otherwise.

If you’re skimming: this doc is the minimal repeatable plan to run small, fast SLO adoption pilots across product teams. Not a full rollout — build artifacts that can be copied and iterate.
summary: Mini-program plan for rapid SLO adoption pilots: 6-week crawl-walk-run with repeatable checklist, roles, artifacts, and low-friction shortcuts.
